quests.title: Procrustes' Iron Bed

dialogue.t: (It won't budge. It seems it will only open when the <color=#00E1FFFF>appointed time</color> arrives...)

dialogue.sit:
"The bell tolls again."
You hear a cold voice say:
"No matter how many times this happens, you cannot stop it..."
"You cannot stop any of it..."

dialogue.t: ...{NICKNAME}... {NICKNAME}!

dialogue.sit: We're in a loop...

dialogue.t: Mm... are we...? Ah... right...
Ugh, Paimon's head suddenly feels so fuzzy... But if we're awake again, then...
Then the ritual isn't finished yet.
Miss Aksinya is still holding Pavlina off for now...
Then we'd better hurry. We need to get that fragment back before Pavlina gets here.
(It won't budge. It seems it will only open when the <color=#00E1FFFF>appointed time</color> arrives...)

dialogue.sit:
"The bell tolls again."
You hear a cold voice say:
"No matter how many times this happens, you cannot stop it..."
"You cannot stop any of it..."

dialogue.t: ...{NICKNAME}... {NICKNAME}!
Whew — there you are! Did the bell wake you? You were completely out. Is the bed here really that comfy?

dialogue.sit: No, Paimon... We've already been through this...

dialogue.t: Huh? Oh... right. Paimon knew this felt familiar...
Ah, Paimon remembers now. The bell rang eight times... and then we...
Wound up right back here.
Oh, Goggles...
It is the ritual taking place here... It repeats over and over...
Until Pavlina, princess of the Snegurochka, has drained every last bit of power from the fragment of my body.
Then, does that mean she's already completed the ritual? Are we too late?
...Have you not succeeded yet?
Seems I'll have to hold on a little longer... It seems Pavlina does not need to maintain the ritual that causes the mansion to loop...
The good news is... that any ritual she does not perform will not result in a "full restoration." Things that you modified in a previous cycle cannot be wholly reset...
Similarly, she could not absorb any power from that last cycle... We do happen to be evenly matched within the Shadow Realm at the moment, after all...

dialogue.sit: So I suppose we're not too late?

dialogue.t: ...Not this time, at least.
Still, I cannot say how much longer I can last. Three cycles? Four?
Before I... Before my strength fails, you must... *sigh* Time runs short.
But... looks like the ritual isn't over yet.
Let's go get that fragment back!
...{NICKNAME}... {NICKNAME}!
Whew — there you are! Did the bell wake you? You were completely out. Is the bed here really that comfy?

dialogue.sit: I think I had a dream.

dialogue.t: No wonder. You were asleep for a long time. Paimon's been keeping watch the whole while. Was it a nice dream, or a scary one?
Actually, never mind. Tell Paimon later. Now's not really the time.
Do you remember what happened earlier? We came to the House of Hesperides for a wedding.

dialogue.sit: But that "ritual" wasn't a wedding at all.

dialogue.t: That towering princess of the Snegurochka, Pavlina... She nearly killed Ikhor...
Paimon knows Ikhor isn't really human, strictly speaking. He's just a fragment of the power that originally belonged to Goggles. But even so...
Compassion is something to be respected, Miss Paimon.

dialogue.sit: They've been carrying out this "ritual" again and again.

dialogue.t: Is... is that what was happening?
So that's what you saw in your dream?
{NICKNAME}... please stay calm. This is to be expected. Pavlina is a fae, after all... She can't draw all the power from my body fragment at once.
So she has to do it bit by bit, through the ritual again and again... That's what the Snegovik's ritual is: they take a soul from someone they love, to make themselves whole.
...Snegovik are fae created without flesh and blood, and thus their souls are incomplete.
Snegovik are fae born for love...
Rather, they are fae who can only become whole through love... by taking another's soul.
...That is why so many love stories centered on Snegovik end in tragedy.
How could that happen? Thank goodness... Actually, thank goodness Goggles was there. We never would've made it out of that wedding without him.
Thanks, Goggles. When Pavlina cast her spell, Goggles was the one who protected us and brought us here, somewhere safe.
While you were asleep, Paimon did some poking around. Looks like someone named Myshkin used to live here. Didn't Aglaya mention him when she first welcomed us?
...*cough* Hello? Do you copy? You should be able to hear what I'm saying, I think.

*sigh* Thanks for nothing, you two. I poured so much effort into getting "him" out, even if in part... Only for you to send him right back, as if nothing had happened. Pavlina almost won right there and then.

dialogue.sit: Huh? You're...

dialogue.t: ...Hmm. It's been a while since we last met, eh, dear colleague? Don't you think you're getting "a bit too passionate" right now?
Ah, sorry, that wasn't meant for you. I'm currently busy dealing with that crazy shrew... How tragic, Pavlina of the Snegovik. You've completely lost it.
Her gaze is like Prime Ice, but her mind is like a powderkeg. A single spark could set her off and destroy all around her.
In any case, I know what you want. We have the same goal.
I've trapped Pavlina, but have little time for anything else right now. Take "his" fragments away from here, one by one, while her grip on this area is weakened, away from her grasp.
This mansion... I came here often in the past... I shall provide you with the map in a while.
Get moving. I won't be able to hold out for long. Finish your business before the clock strikes eight times. Before the wedding, or perhaps everything else, starts all over again...
Hello??? Hello...? She's gone...
Take Goggles' fragments... one by one? What does she even mean? Doesn't she know that Pavlina has some of Goggles' power too???

dialogue.sit: She may have something else up her sleeves too.

dialogue.t: Yeah... Better take what she says with a huge rock of salt. But what should we do now then?
Hey, you know what? This is about Goggles! We should ask what he wants.
I think... Maybe we should gather at least some of the power that has been split up, and try to make him as complete as possible. Then we can take it all back.
This may sound a little ironic, but my wish is for the fragments, incomplete as they are, to be as whole as possible...
It's just like how the Snegurochka princess must have decided to perform the ritual because she wanted to help her people become more "whole."
And that is something I can understand, and even empathize with, to some degree.
How can you feel for her!? She was gonna gobble you up, piece by piece, just to get what she wanted!!!
Paimon can share her food or Mora with other folks, no problem. But if you want Paimon to hand over an arm or a leg...
Or even Paimon's hair! Hmm... Actually, hair seems alright... especially if it's just a few strands — Anyway, that's not the point.
It doesn't matter what the other person's reasons are. This is something... something Paimon needs to think over! Very carefully! Though Paimon probably won't say yes anyway, to be honest...

dialogue.sit: Yes. It's not good to over-deplete yourself for the sake of others.

dialogue.t: ...You are right. But that aside, there is another reason we must reclaim him "whole."
Another reason? And what would that be?

dialogue.sit: That you don't need to know, Paimon.

dialogue.t: Huh? Are the two of you keeping something from Paimon!? And Paimon's not talking about secret snack stashes or anything like tha——

dialogue.sit: We should get moving.

dialogue.t: I have marked the fragment locations. Let's go, before the clock strikes eight.

dialogue.sit: Huh? Aksinya?

dialogue.t: Ha! I am the creator of the Eye of Graeae, after all. I can still make use of some of its functions.
...Hmm. It's been a while since we last met, eh, dear colleague? Don't you think you're getting "a bit too passionate" right now?
Ah, sorry, that wasn't meant for you. I'm currently busy dealing with that crazy shrew... How tragic, Pavlina of the Snegovik. You've completely lost it.

That's the only way to ensure that shrew won't be able to offer up "his" power for her people.
We have to take back all that power, don't we? It's not the same as why she seeks your power, is it? "To have a body once more"... that's what "he" wants, isn't it?
Then go. This mansion... I came here often in the past... I shall provide you with the map in a while.

dialogue.sit: We should get moving.

dialogue.t: I have marked the fragment locations. Let's go, before the clock strikes eight.
Who are you people? And what are you doing here in this room?
Oh? You must be Aglaya. We, uh, we've already shown our invite earlier...
Is that so? But how do you know my name...? Ah, you must have heard it from the others.
Alright then. I'm guessing someone has already told you about the dos and don'ts around here.
But this room is... also off-limits... Ahem. This isn't a room for ordinary guests.
The ritual will begin when <color=#00E1FFFF>the clock strikes eight times</color>. I wish the both of you a most pleasant and unforgettable day here at the House of Hesperides.

dialogue.sit: Aglaya leaves...

dialogue.t: The way she was acting, it was like she had never met us before... That's weird. Is it because... everything has restarted?
I'm not sure why you did that... but it does cause us some trouble.
Please don't do anything so dangerous again.
(It won't budge. It seems it will only open when the <color=#00E1FFFF>appointed time</color> arrives...)
Are you okay? How do you feel now?
He may have a body now, but he is still only a puppet. He cannot feel anything so complex, nor can he answer you.
Paimon knows, but still... It's not like it hurts to ask. Just let Paimon be.
Like I said before, your compassion is something to be respected. That kindness is one of your virtues.
But I don't think {NICKNAME} would want it to end up hurting you.
What do you mean...? Wait, does this have something to do with what you were all hiding from Paimon earlier?
You... really are an odd one. You are me. But it's something I've only realized today.
That is because my presence has become more evident now that the princess is no longer in the way.

dialogue.sit: How does it feel to converse with yourself?

dialogue.t: More ordinary than I'd ever imagined. Even if I was fortunate enough to have a body right now, I doubt we'd be throwing our arms around each other and crying.
This body won't shed a tear, for it is created out of Prime Ice.
Yes. That, I am aware.
Ah, that's right. You may not possess form, but you have something that I don't... reason and intelligence.
Um, could we pick up this conversation again a little later? We've got to get somewhere safe now. Who knows when Pavlina is coming back...
Although, she still has one of the fragments with her... That's right. What are we gonna do about that fragment?
Do we talk her out of the ritual? That doesn't seem very possible... She hasn't exactly been open to persuasion so far.
Is defeating her the only way then? Not that Paimon doesn't have trust in {NICKNAME} or anything...
...Do you seek to stop the ritual?
Mmhmm! If that ritual continues, you'll be finished! Finito! Dunzo!
Paimon knows that you're not really human, and your uh, form of existence is different from ours. But we cannot possibly sit back and watch you get wiped out by her.
I apologize, but I'm afraid I cannot assist with this wish of yours.
Huh? Why?

The ritual has long been set in motion. Though the taboo that must not be inquired into or spoken of has already been broken, the ritual has fallen into distortion... It can neither be halted nor reversed.
The only course remaining to me is to become one with it... or fade entirely into the ether.
What!?!? But without you, Goggles will never be whole again...
But if the ritual were to continue...
This is neither death nor the end. It is a return, a birth. If all goes well, all the Snegovik under her protection will receive a new lease of life.

dialogue.sit: Is that what you really believe, or what she made you believe?

dialogue.t: Y—Yeah... Paimon remembers how you never pushed back on anything, not even once, when we first met you. Are you sure she didn't put this idea in your head, too?
Strangely, my mind feels remarkably clear at present, and I find myself recalling certain things from the past.
We were once companions who shared the same ambition... And we were willing to pay the price for a love set free, for the sake of that "more perfect world" of her dreams.
Of course, it is natural that one pays a price for their dreams to come true. Yet even if you have finally made your choice, the path ahead will not be an easy one either.
And eventually, she simply disappeared somewhere along the way, among the countless refinements and ascensions...
She had even forgotten that I once chose to do all of this, without need of shackles.
...You do know that you will not succeed.
I have neither your reason nor your intelligence, and I cannot predict things that have yet to happen.
Is that the thing you were reluctant to tell Paimon??? That's ridiculous... Are you sure there's no other way?

Just as the dew upon leaf and flower inevitably finds its way back to the stream, so too is the path toward becoming one irreversible. Once a single drop has returned to the waters, there is no way it can be reclaimed.
But nevertheless, I thank you for your... consideration. I now understand why the other "me" chose to travel with you.
...Hey! I do hope the two of you have sent out the fragments like I said, since I am in quite the predicament now myself.
I'm trapped here, and shall have to be away for a while... That was quite the move. I will leave the rest to you.
I should go now. She's here for me.

quests.description: The so-called wedding at the House of Hesperides turns out to be less delightful than expected. Pavlina tries to sacrifice Ikhor for her wish, though she is fortunately thwarted by Aksinya in the end. Pavlina is also thrown into the Shadow Realm, where she will continue to face off with Aksinya…
